title: The Search for Life
objective: After this level you can describe how scientists look for signs of life beyond Earth.
summary: Scientists hunt for biosignatures on Mars, in ocean moons and in exoplanet air, and SETI listens for signals. None confirmed yet.

cards.headline: Are we alone? We finally have tools that could answer.
cards.body: Nobody knows yet. But the search has a plan: follow the water nearby, and read the air far away.

cards.headline: Close to home
cards.body: In our own solar system, the search follows the water. On Mars, NASA’s Perseverance rover is collecting rock samples in Jezero Crater, the site of an ancient lake. Farther out, ocean moons like Europa and Enceladus keep liquid water under their ice. Why there? Liquid water, a source of energy and the right chemistry are the key ingredients for life as we know it. Call it life’s recipe card.

cards.headline: Reading alien air
cards.body: Around other stars, scientists read the air instead. They look for biosignatures: gases, such as oxygen and methane together, that living things could produce. The James Webb Space Telescope can analyze starlight passing through some exoplanets’ atmospheres to detect the gases they contain. It’s a sniff test done with light, from light-years away.

cards.fact: No life has yet been confirmed anywhere beyond Earth.
cards.context: Not on Mars, not in the ocean moons, not in any alien air. Meanwhile, SETI projects listen for another kind of clue: radio and other signals a technological civilization could send. For now, Earth is the only place we know of with life.

cards.headline: Search for life: underway
learned: Scientists search Mars and ocean moons for signs of life
Biosignatures are gases life could produce
No life beyond Earth is confirmed yet

options.label: A radio signal from aliens
options.rationale: That would be a technosignature, SETI’s target.

options.label: A fossil found on Earth
options.rationale: Biosignatures are signs of life elsewhere.

options.label: The signature on a space mission
A sign, like certain gases, that life might be present

questions.explanation: A biosignature is evidence, such as oxygen and methane together, that life could be producing.

questions.prompt: How can Webb study an exoplanet’s atmosphere without visiting it?

options.label: By analyzing starlight that passes through the atmosphere
By listening to its radio signals

questions.explanation: Gases in the atmosphere absorb specific wavelengths of the starlight passing through, leaving fingerprints Webb can read.

questions.prompt: From Level 47: why are Europa and Enceladus high on the list of places to look for life?

options.label: They are the warmest worlds in the solar system
They have liquid water, energy and the right chemistry
They are the closest moons to Earth

questions.explanation: These moons hide liquid water oceans heated by tidal flexing: key ingredients for life as we know it.
